title: Workload Curator: continuous batch parameter recommendations and safe-apply guardrails
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build a lightweight Workload Curator service that continuously analyzes per-customer inference traces and recommends batching and caching parameter changes, and provides a safe-apply path with automated rollback.
description.2: Background: existing autotune components surface batch size suggestions but lack workload drift detection and a conservative safe-apply mechanism. We want an engine that reasons over cost/latency trade-offs, KV/prefix cache hit interplay, and hardware-specific kernel costs to produce concrete config diffs for each route/model combination.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Curator produces per-route recommendation artifacts (batch size, max latency SLO, KV cache TTL/confidence) with estimated cost delta and risk score.
2) Recommendations are surfaced to Console as a reviewable diff and can be applied via a shadow-apply and gradual roll-forward.
3) Safe-apply pipeline includes circuit-breakers: latency spike detection, error-rate thresholds, and automatic rollback to previous config.
4) Telemetry: compare observed vs predicted token/sec, mean P95 latency, and unit cost; surface mismatch >10% as "regression alerts".
5) A runbook for manual intervention and a one-click rollback in Console.
6) Integration tests (shadow-apply) running against synthetic workloads and replay traces with deterministic rollbacks.
design_notes:
Heuristics: combine fingerprinted workload clusters (sequence length, prompt rate, warm cache fraction) with empirical cost curves to recommend conservative batch horizons. Use a 3-tier risk model (low/medium/high) computed from latency headroom, cache sensitivity, and historical variance.
Profiling: sample KV cache hit/miss across prefixes, track per-model KV cache build time, and estimate break-even points for increasing batch size vs cache TTL reduction.
Continuous tuning: anneal batch parameters using exponential backoff when risk is medium and allow faster changes for low-risk profiles.
Safe-apply: always shadow-apply for 1 hour with replicated traffic; then canary 5% traffic for 30 minutes, then 25%, then full, with automatic rollback on threshold breach.
Fallbacks: include quantized model variant fallback and lower-throughput dedicated pool fallback for high-risk recommendations.
Data retention: keep profiling windows for 30 days to detect seasonality and drift.
Privacy: only ingest anonymized traces (no user text), and use aggregated metrics for recommendations (KMS keys applied for stored artifacts).
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (2 sprints): lightweight profiler + offline recommendation generator; schema for recommendation artifacts; Console diff UI prototype.
Phase 2 (3 sprints): shadow-apply pipeline, telemetry comparisons, and canary rollout controller.
Phase 3 (1 sprint): automatic rollback rules, runbook, and e2e integration tests.
Phase 4 (ongoing): tune heuristics, add cost-aware batching knobs, and add ML-based drift detector.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: recommendations cause latency regressions in tails. Mitigation: conservative default risk scoring, mandatory shadow-apply, and P99 circuit-breaker.
Risk: mis-estimated cost savings due to cache dynamics. Mitigation: explicit TTL recommendation and simulated replay to estimate cache build cost.
Risk: operator trust. Mitigation: rich diffs in Console with predicted vs observed charts and clear rollback actions.
notes: We should reuse kernel-selection cost models from infra-team (ENG-613204) and the rollout controller from feature-rollouts (ENG-7412). Coordinate with Security for KMS integration prior to storing recommendation artifacts.
